name: Adversarial Machine Learning
description: Adversarial examples, poisoning, backdoors, evasion, and robustness of ML models.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this area, around 2018, treated adversarial machine learning as a frontier where the threat model itself was still being mapped out. Some papers turned attacks into tools, like "Turning Your Weakness Into a Strength: Watermarking Deep Neural Networks by Backdooring" (2018), which repurposed backdoors to claim ownership of models, while "Formal Security Analysis of Neural Networks using Symbolic Intervals" (2018) pushed toward provable robustness. At the same time, "When Does Machine Learning FAIL? Generalized Transferability for Evasion and Poisoning Attacks" (2018) systematized how attacks transfer across models, and "AttriGuard" (2018) flipped adversarial perturbations into a privacy defense. The common thread was establishing that ML systems were genuinely attackable in security-critical settings.

Through 2019 to 2021, the field broadened from image classifiers into the messy realities of deployed pipelines and new domains. Attacks moved up the stack and into the physical and pre-processing layers, as in "Seeing is Not Believing: Camouflage Attacks on Image Scaling Algorithms" (2019) and hardware-level "DeepHammer" (2020) bit-flip attacks. Poisoning matured beyond toy settings to target real training supply chains: "Explanation-Guided Backdoor Poisoning Attacks Against Malware Classifiers" (2021) abused crowdsourced threat feeds, and "Poisoning the Unlabeled Dataset of Semi-Supervised Learning" (2021) showed that even unlabeled data was a liability. Defenses kept pace across modalities, with "T-Miner" (2021) for text trojans and "WaveGuard" (2021) for audio adversarial examples.

By 2022 to 2023 the center of gravity shifted to distributed and generative settings. "FLAME: Taming Backdoors in Federated Learning" (2022) addressed the hard problem of backdoors when training is decentralized, and attacks reached pre-training itself with "PoisonedEncoder: Poisoning the Unlabeled Pre-training Data in Contrastive Learning" (2022). The rise of diffusion and deepfake models reframed adversarial perturbations as a protective shield, most visibly in "Glaze: Protecting Artists from Style Mimicry by Text-to-Image Models" (2023), while physical-world attacks grew more sophisticated and targeted, as in "TPatch: A Triggered Physical Adversarial Patch" (2023).

Most recently, in 2024, the agenda has followed the field's pivot to large language models. "Instruction Backdoor Attacks Against Customized LLMs" (2024) and "An LLM-Assisted Easy-to-Trigger Backdoor Attack on Code Completion Models" (2024) show backdoor and poisoning ideas migrating from pixels and audio to prompts, instructions, and generated code, signaling that the next phase of adversarial ML research is squarely about LLM-based systems and their downstream deployments.

milestones.title: Turning Your Weakness Into a Strength: Watermarking Deep Neural Networks by Backdooring
milestones.note: reframed backdoors constructively as a model-ownership watermarking primitive, an early and widely-cited foundation

milestones.title: When Does Machine Learning FAIL? Generalized Transferability for Evasion and Poisoning Attacks
milestones.note: systematized how evasion and poisoning attacks transfer across models, framing the early threat landscape

milestones.title: DeepHammer: Depleting the Intelligence of Deep Neural Networks through Targeted Chain of Bit Flips
milestones.note: pushed adversarial ML below the algorithm into hardware bit-flip attacks on deployed models

milestones.title: Explanation-Guided Backdoor Poisoning Attacks Against Malware Classifiers
milestones.note: demonstrated practical poisoning of real security pipelines via crowdsourced threat feeds

milestones.title: FLAME: Taming Backdoors in Federated Learning
milestones.note: tackled backdoor defense in the harder decentralized federated setting, a heavily-cited shift

milestones.title: Glaze: Protecting Artists from Style Mimicry by Text-to-Image Models
milestones.note: turned adversarial perturbations into a real-world defense against generative model style mimicry

milestones.title: Instruction Backdoor Attacks Against Customized LLMs
milestones.note: marked the migration of backdoor attacks into the LLM era of customized models
